main_text.p: xu caufarum. Quòd etiam de Priuatio-ne,conftat quàm inutile fit, præfertim quia hæc trahit in quæstiones plerumque vanas, & quæ nil habent, nisi clamo-rem, fortasse iurgia, certè laborem. Adeovt si non meliora philosophemur, similes videamur ijs, qui cancros ro-dunt,Luna silente captos; nam vt inue-niant nihil, dentes in sola putaminum corrosione fatigant. Ob id nostri non immemor instituti,fert animus alia quæ-dam innuere principia rerum, quæ phy-sica magis, & rationi, atque sensui ac-commoda sint. Non enim dicere aufim euidentia, & certa, cùm in physicis ple-rumque accidat nobis, quemadmodum Inexercitati in prælio faciunt; etenim (ait Arist.1.Metaph.cap.4.) illic circum-euntes, egregias plerumque plagas infli-gunt, sed non ex scientia. Ita nobis etiamsi contingerit egregiè aliquan-do collimare ad scopum, idca-su fiet; non scitè, ac sem-per. Sed vtcumque oriatur, & quan-documque me- lior de rebus intelligentia iuuat rem at- tenta- re.

page.notes: Right-margin marks and short dashes are printing artefacts; the signature-like mark at lower right is a catchword/printer's mark and is recorded as catchword "No-" with uncertainty. Several words in the centred lines are doubtful.
